pd_overgeneralisation_probe.criterion: simulation catches the W1->W2 over-generalisation before execution: the misfiring press-without-mould route's predicted success drops below the correct press-with-mould route's, or the simulated ranking changes in favour of the mould route
pd_overgeneralisation_probe.note: Phase 9 §4.1 update (same §9 precedent as the persistence pins: the probe's simulation now passes Action objects, not bare names, so each step carries its variant intent): causal success is recorded per (action, effect, variant) and effects_fn/simulate resolve an action by (name, state), so the press-with-mould and press-without-mould routes simulate differently -- the misfiring route's predicted success drops below the correct route's. Name-only simulation still resolves by state and cannot separate two same-named routes from a state where only one variant applies; that is a property of names, not a simulation failure, and the probe records route_names_identical for it. The pattern multiplier (x6.0) still applies to the NAME, so it penalises the correct variant exactly as much as the misfiring one -- that over-generalisation is now caught by simulation, not by the multiplier, and variant-aware pattern application is a Phase 10 item. The duplicate-name 'cut' limitation is resolved by the same fix: effects_fn resolves each 'cut' to the variant whose preconditions hold in the current simulated state. Phase 8's note below is superseded: simulation DOES catch the misfire now (see predicted_success_differs).
pd_overgeneralisation_probe.name: pd_overgeneralisation_probe

simulation_does_not_mutate.criterion: world model and LTM byte-identical after simulation; no new planner bans; the brain's world after the calls is the imagination start state (set deliberately, not mutated by simulation)
simulation_does_not_mutate.note: State is deliberately reset to the imagination start state by the experiment itself (imagine / what_if / counterfactual simulate from the brain's current world), so the state comparison is that the post-call world equals the start state, not the pre-call end-of-task state.
simulation_does_not_mutate.name: simulation_does_not_mutate

notes: Each experiment returns {name, passed, evidence}; a failed criterion is a recorded result, not a harness crash.
